To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

transgenic introduction of androgens in estrogen-receptor-, progestrin-receptor-, androgen-receptor-, breast cancer cells renders these cell lines responsive to hormonal manipulation, and that the introduction of androgrens into these cells is associated with increased cell proliferation.

the expression of the androgen receptor (AR) in ER-negative breast cancer cells can render them responsive to androgen receptor antagonists, such as bicalutamide and enzalutamide, and that the combination of bicalutamide with enzalutamate or with the antiestrogen fulvestrant can further increase the efficacy.

(1) The androgen receptor (AR) is a potential therapeutic target for ER-negative/HER2-positive (HER2+) breast cancer; and (2) the AR inhibitor, enzalutamide, is an effective treatment for ER-negative/AR-positive (AR+) and ER-negative/AR-negative (AR-) breast cancer cells.
